findings.text: VMX exit reason numbers for early events are fixed small integers with gaps: exception or NMI 0, external interrupt 1, triple fault 2, INIT 3, SIPI 4, other SMI 6, interrupt window 7, NMI window 8, task switch 9, CPUID 10, HLT 12, INVD 13, INVLPG 14, RDPMC 15, RDTSC 16, VMCALL 18, VMCLEAR 19, VMLAUNCH 20, VMPTRLD 21, VMPTRST 22, VMREAD 23, VMRESUME 24, VMWRITE 25, VMOFF 26, VMON 27, control register access 28, debug register access 29, IO instruction 30, MSR read 31 and MSR write 32.

Later VMX exit reason numbers continue with gaps: invalid state 33, MSR load fail 34, MWAIT 36, monitor trap flag 37, MONITOR 39, PAUSE 40, machine check during entry 41, TPR below threshold 43, APIC access 44, EOI induced 45, GDTR or IDTR 46, LDTR or TR 47, EPT violation 48, EPT misconfig 49, INVEPT 50, RDTSCP 51, preemption timer 52, INVVPID 53, WBINVD 54, XSETBV 55, APIC write 56, RDRAND 57, INVPCID 58, VMFUNC 59, ENCLS 60, RDSEED 61, PML full 62, XSAVES 63, XRSTORS 64, UMWAIT 67, TPAUSE 68, bus lock 74, notify 75, SEAMCALL 76, TDCALL 77, immediate MSR read 84 and immediate MSR write 85.

VMX exit status carries two flag bits and three abort codes: failed entry is the top bit 0x80000000, SGX enclave mode is bit 27 value 0x08000000, save guest MSR failure is 1, load host PDPTE failure is 2, load host MSR failure is 4. The header also defines paired number to short name tables for reasons and for the failed entry flag.

Legacy vsyscall identifiers are an ordered triple starting at zero: vgettimeofday then vtime then vgetcpu. The vsyscall page address is defined as negative ten shifted left by twenty, placing it near the top of the canonical address range.

Cache maintenance helpers are exported for cross-CPU use: run writeback invalidate on one named CPU, on all CPUs, or on a supplied CPU mask, plus writeback without invalidate on all CPUs or on a supplied mask. Each public helper delegates to a tiny local routine that issues the corresponding cache instruction.

Cache helpers pass no payload and request synchronous execution: the dummy pointer is unused and the wait behavior is requested. The mask variants apply only to the supplied set while the all-CPU variants apply everywhere.

32-bit 64-bit atomics built on 8-byte compare exchange provide read, set, exchange, decrement only when positive, add unless equal, and increment only when nonzero. Read loads the pair, set and exchange store through a retry loop, and the conditional forms snapshot then attempt an update only when the guard holds.

Atomic compare exchange loops retry on mismatch. Decrement-if-positive leaves negative inputs unchanged and reports the prior value; add-unless reports success or equality without storing on match; increment-not-zero leaves zero unchanged and reports whether it stored.

Emulated wide compare exchange entry points cover normal and per-CPU memory for 8-byte and 16-byte widths. Each compares the memory pair against the expected pair, stores the new pair on equality, otherwise loads memory into the expected registers.

Emulated compare exchange signals outcome through the zero flag in saved flags and preserves interrupt state around a disabled window: success sets the flag, failure clears it, and flags are restored before return.

Page clearing provides a bulk unrolled 64-byte-step routine and a size-tiered store-alternative routine. The former scales its iteration count down by the block size; the latter selects unrolled stores for at least 64 bytes, word stores for at least 8 bytes, and byte stores for the tail.

Store-alternative clearing is fault tolerant: every multi-byte store has a fixup that resumes at byte-tail clearing, and the unrolled path may store some tail bytes twice after a fault. Exact remaining length is recovered by the byte loop rather than by trusting pointer or count adjustments.

Boolean command line search scans bounded input through word start, word compare and word skip states. A match requires the full option text followed by whitespace or end of input; it returns the one-based position after the leading separator, returns zero for no match or overrun, and negative one for absent input.

Valued command line search adds a buffer copy state entered only on option text immediately followed by equals. It copies until whitespace or end, counts full value length even when truncating, always terminates when buffer size is nonzero, and returns negative one for absent input or negative length when never matched.

Command line parsing treats every byte at or below ASCII space as separator, never reads past the supplied maximum length, tolerates missing termination, and wrapper helpers fall back to a built-in command line only when the primary lookup did not succeed and a boolean configuration path is active.

Fragile machine-check copy exposes an enable operation that turns on a static branch and a tail helper that copies forward one byte at a time until length is exhausted or one byte reports failure, returning the number of bytes not copied.

Branch-history isolation argument scrubbing provides aligned variants for zero through seven logical arguments plus a global end marker. Each variant either returns directly or conditionally overwrites that many argument registers from a scratch register, with unreachable trap blocks shared between neighboring variants.

Atomicity uses bus locking only where an update must be indivisible: exchange and conditional 64-bit updates prefix the compare exchange, while plain aligned loads and stores rely on processor atomicity. Emulated wide updates instead disable interrupts around a non-atomic load-compare-store sequence.

Callers must not assume single-copy behavior for faulting clears or emulated wide atomics under concurrency: the clear path can write bytes twice after a fault, and emulated compare exchange is only atomic with respect to interrupts on the executing CPU, not against other CPUs.
